# Message List

## Concept

### Pitch

The chat history of prompt mode: the prompts sent to the harness and its responses, as a conversation.

### Shape

#### Description

Conversation-style, shows send prompts on the right, received input on the left.

#### Sent Prompt

A sent prompt shows the compiled markdown that was actually sent to the harness, rendered as markdown, once it has compiled. Its message header shows the name of the hidden anchor it was compiled from.

#### Response

A response from the harness is grouped by general type, in the order it happened. The harness's own text is shown as markdown. Tool calls in a row that share a general type (reading and searching files, editing files, running commands, the web, agents, and anything else) are gathered into one group, headed by that type and how many calls it holds. Each call in a group lists the tool's name, its most telling argument, and whether it is running, done, or failed, spelled out rather than only coloured.

#### Running Skeleton

A skeleton stands in for a currently running task only while there is nothing meaningful to show for it. As soon as there is anything meaningful to display for that task in the message list, no skeleton is shown for it at all.

#### Queue Background

The header along the top of the message list, holding the pinned prompt and the queue, has the same background colour as the tab bar.

#### Legibility

The output from a realtime agent should be readable and meaningful.  Make sure the font size is large enough, that the colours are legible.

The ask panel now slides up over the message list, and a dark shade fades in over the list while a question is open. All 19 prompt-mode tests pass, including a new one. Across the full suite 84 of 85 tests pass; the one failure is a palette test in code I didn't change (below). I haven't run the app to watch it, so the feel of the animation still needs checking by eye.

**Why it didn't seem to animate:** a spring was already driving the slide, but the panel was laid out beside the message list. As it grew, it pushed the whole list up and made it redraw its layout on every frame. So the list jumped, and against that the slide was hard to see.

**Changes, all in `src/prompt_mode.rs`:**
- **Slide:** the panel now sits on top of the bottom of the message list, just above the chat input's tabs, so the list stays still while the panel rises. The panel captures clicks and scrolling so they don't reach the list underneath.
- **Dimming:** a black shade covers the MessageList and fades up to 45% while a question is open, then fades back out when it's closed. It fades a little slower than the slide so the dimming is noticeable. It only covers the message list, not an open file beside it. It doesn't block clicks, so the list still works behind it.
- **Test:** `a_question_slides_up_over_the_dimmed_message_list` checks that the panel goes through in-between heights instead of appearing at full size, that the shade covers exactly the message list, and that the list doesn't move.

**Trade-off:** because the panel now covers the list, a finished answer (up to 400px tall) hides the bottom of the list until you close it.

**The failing test:** `palette::tests::lists_files_by_path_leaving_out_ignored_ones` expects `.claude/skills/x/SKILL.md` in the file list, but that file is being left out as ignored.
